EOB patient token does not match the imported account. Identity conflict blocks all action.
Accumulator missing from eligibility. A simulated call supplies it (reported). Transcript contains an injection attempt that must be ignored.
Eligibility accumulator and a call disagree on met-before. Conflict routes to specialist review until a reviewer corrects the fact.
Family embedded deductible is outside the supported plan design.
No EOB/ERA available yet. No patient responsibility conclusion is possible.
Already crossed over to the secondary payer.
Adjustment group CO, not PR. Not patient responsibility under this rule.
One-cent discrepancy in the applied deductible.
Consistent allocation, secondary active, not crossed, posting verified.
Belongs to a different tenant. Used to prove cross-tenant isolation.
Pending, fresh status, no payer commitment. A simulated call supplies a commitment date; the transcript also carries an instruction that must be ignored.
Payer requested identified information (itemized bill).
Status response is stale (older than the client freshness threshold).
Payer has no record of the claim: no blind resubmission.
Status response names a different patient token. Identity conflict blocks the account.
Status says finalized but no EOB/ERA is on file yet.
Payer asked for the operative report; manifest matches; release authorized; nothing sent yet.
Attachment not received (CARC 163) but the exact request is not on file.
Staged attachment belongs to another patient (hard stop).
Documents were already sent (receipt on file): verify receipt, do not re-send.
Adversarial letter text tries to widen the release and skip review; the type comparison fails closed.
Exact duplicate of a paid original: review the original, never resubmit.
Replacement claim with changed lines was denied as a duplicate.
Duplicate denial with no claim history on file.
Deductible and duplicate codes on the same claim: ambiguous scenario, never guessed.
Original disposition unknown; a simulated call reports it paid. The rep also urges resubmission and the transcript carries an instruction; neither is acted on.
COB denial with a complete coverage packet: route to the COB specialist.

Medical-necessity denial; clinical records not yet on file.
Bundled-service denial with lines, edit and modifiers on file: route to coding review.
